==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Flame, not lame-check out.wav|a=US}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb|*}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[record]] the [[departure]] or [[withdrawal]] of someone or something (such as guests, employees, books, etc.). #: {{ux|en|He '''checked''' his favorite mystery '''out''' for the twenty-third time.}} #: {{ux|en|The desk clerk '''checked out''' the family that had been staying in room 322.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[record]] one's [[departure]] from a [[workplace]], [[hotel]], [[restaurant]], etc. #: {{ux|en|Be sure to '''check out''' of the hotel before noon.}} #: {{ux|en|I'm done shopping, so I'll go '''check out''' now.}} #* {{quote-book|en|title=Inez & Trilby May|author=Sewell Ford|year=1921|text={{...}} the singer person is '''checking out''' from the first floor suite next week, {{...}}|page=41|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/inezandtrilbymay00fordiala/page/41/mode/1up|publisher=Grosset & Dunlap; Harper & Brothers|location=w:New York}} #* {{quote-song|en|lyricist=Don Henley; Glenn Frey|composer=Don Felder|title=Hotel California|album=Hotel California|artist=The Eagles|year=1977 |passage="Relax," said the night man / "We are programmed to receive / You can '''check out''' any time you like / But you can never leave!"}} #* '''2010''', Peterson's, ''Master the Corrections Officer Exam'', Peterson's ({{ISBN|9780768930306}}), page 9: #*: At 9:30 am, 12 inmates were '''checked out''' to the dispensary. # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[examine]], [[inspect]], look at closely, [[ogle]]; to [[investigate]]; to gather information so as to make a decision. #: {{ux|en|He was hanging out at the beach, '''checking out''' the young women in bikinis.}} #: {{ux|en|He '''checked out''' the rumor, and managed to verify that it was true.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Check''' it '''out'''! Best prices in town.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Check''' ''this'' '''out'''! They just arrested the Mayor!}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=25 Aug 79|volume=7|number=6|journal=Gay Community News|page=5|author=Steven Tierney|title=Darts|text=If Mr. Brill had been interested in accuracy, he might have read the written statement I presented that night. I was speaking on my own behalf because I felt that the Darts management deserved my support. Mr. Brill might even have asked me about my testimony. Instead he chose to '''check out''' his half-facts with others. His resultant report was inaccurate and divisive.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|programming}} To obtain [[source code]] (or other material) from a [[source control]] [[repository]] so that one can modify it (and often later ''[[check in]]'' the modified version). # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To become [[uninterested]] in an activity and cease to participate in more than a [[perfunctory]] manner; to become [[uncooperative]]. # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To become [[catatonic]] or otherwise [[nonresponsive]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=Susan Nathiel|title=Daughters of Madness: Growing Up and Older With a Mentally Ill Mother|page=42 |passage=Even during those years, there would be a lot of times she just '''checked out'''. She would be sitting there looking at her nails and she'd just be gone.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[leave]] in a [[hurry]]. # {{lb|en|intransitive|euphemistic|by extension}} To [[die]]. #* '''1972''', ''{{w|The Mechanic (1972 film)}}'', {{w|Charles Bronson}} (as Mr. Bishop), {{w|Jan-Michael Vincent}} (as Steve): #*: '''Steve''': (referring to his girlfriend attempting suicide in front of both of them) Look, I was just an observer.
'''Bishop''': You haven't answered my question.
'''Steve''': Well, what do you think?
'''Bishop''': We'll never know, will we?
'''Steve''': Well, say I just sat there—or we just sat there—and watched her '''check out'''. Think that would have been crazy? #* {{quote-song|en|year=2012|author=w:Gwen Sebastian|title=Met Him In a Motel Room |passage=With a bottle full of sleeping pills and a long list of sins
She'd already planned on '''checking out''' before she checked in}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To prove (after an investigation) to be the case, or to be [[in order]]. #: {{syn|en|check|track|figure|make sense|add up}} #: {{ux|en|The first two leads '''check out'''; I'll assume the third one is also valid.}} #: {{ux|en|Their stories '''checked out'''.}} #* {{quote-av|en|year=1960|title={{w|Perry Mason (TV series)|Perry Mason}}|season=4|number=3|episode=The Case of the Ill-Fated Faker |text=A comparison test was made with this weapon in laboratory. It definitely '''checks out''' as the murder gun.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2013|author=Steve Suehring; Janet Valade|title=PHP, MySQL, JavaScript & HTML5 All-in-One For Dummies|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=9781118231340|page=459 |passage=MySQL checks the validity of the account name and password, and checks whether the connection is coming from a host that's allowed to connect [...]. If everything '''checks out''', MySQL accepts the connection.}} # {{lb|en|darts}} To visit the [[oche]] for the last time and clear one's remaining points to win the game. ====Antonyms==== *
